title: Pre-call research in 90 seconds
problem: Reps rebuild context from a dozen tabs before every call: news, org changes, the annual report and whatever is buried in the CRM.
value: One prompt pulls public and internal context into a one-page call plan with three angles to lead with and the opening question to ask.
prompt: For {account}, combine the last 90 days of news, the risk section of the latest 10-K and our Salesforce notes. Give me the 3 priorities their CEO keeps talking about, 2 risks we can help with, and the opening question I should ask {persona}.

title: Deal review prep from call recordings
problem: Front-line managers listen to hours of calls to find the real risk in a deal before each review.
value: A one-page risk brief per deal, with the buyer quotes that prove each risk and the question to put to the rep.
prompt: From these {call transcripts} and the {opportunity} fields, list the 3 biggest risks to close, the buyer quote behind each one, and the single question I should ask the rep in our deal review.

title: Product launch training video in a day
problem: Launch training lands weeks after the launch, so reps learn the new story from customers.
value: A narrated, on-brand training video ready on launch day, built from the launch brief.
prompt: Turn this {launch brief} into a 90-second training script: the customer problem, what changed, 3 talk tracks and 1 objection with its answer. Then storyboard it as 8 shots with one line of narration each.

title: Follow-up email before you leave the call
problem: Follow-ups go out late and generic, and buyers forget what they agreed to.
value: A recap written in the buyer's own words, with next steps, owners and dates, sent while the call is still fresh.
prompt: From this {call transcript}, write a follow-up to {buyer} that restates their 2 priorities in their own words, confirms next steps with owners and dates, and stays under 140 words.

title: Forecast commentary in one click
problem: Sales leaders hand-write the weekly forecast narrative from spreadsheet exports.
value: A drafted commentary that explains the week's movement in plain language, ready to edit and post to the leadership channel.
prompt: Compare this week's {pipeline export} with last week's. Explain the 5 biggest movements in plain language, flag every slipped close date, and draft a 150-word update for {channel}.

title: Discovery questions from a 10-K
problem: Discovery questions stay generic because nobody has time to read the annual report.
value: Five questions grounded in what the CFO already told investors, each tied to a metric they are measured on.
prompt: Read {10-K}. List the 3 initiatives management committed to and the metric for each. Write 5 discovery questions for {persona} that connect those metrics to {our capability}.

title: Mutual action plan from one transcript
problem: Deals stall in late stage because nobody owns the path to signature.
value: A shared plan with milestones, owners on both sides and dates the buyer can edit with you.
prompt: Draft a mutual action plan for {opportunity} closing on {date}. Work back from signature through security review, legal, procurement and executive sign-off. Name an owner on each side for every step.
beforeText: 1 hour to build a close plan

title: Coaching scorecards on every call
problem: Managers can only review a handful of calls, so coaching depends on luck.
value: Every call scored against the team rubric, with one timestamped coaching moment and a five-minute drill.
prompt: Score this {call} against {rubric}. Give one strength, one moment to coach with its timestamp, and a practice drill that takes under 5 minutes.

title: Objection roleplay with an AI buyer
problem: Reps meet the toughest objections for the first time in front of real buyers.
value: A skeptical AI buyer built from real call objections, available any time, that scores the rep when the roleplay ends.
prompt: Act as {persona} at {account}. Use these real objections from our calls: {objections}. Push back twice before conceding. After 6 turns, score my responses against the {framework} rubric.

title: Win-loss themes from 40 interviews
problem: Win-loss interviews pile up unread, so the pitch never changes.
value: Ranked themes with quotes, by segment, and three concrete changes to make to the talk track.
prompt: Code these {interviews} into win and loss reasons. Rank the themes by frequency and deal size, give 2 quotes for each, and recommend 3 changes to our {talk track}.

title: Battlecards that refresh themselves
problem: Battlecards go stale the week after they ship.
value: A Monday digest of competitor moves with the updated talk track, posted where reps already work.
prompt: Every Monday, scan {sources} for changes at {competitor}. Summarise what changed, update the 3 landmines to set, and post the new talk track to {channel}.

title: A new rep's first week, rebuilt
problem: New hires drown in links and decks in week one and still cannot answer basic customer questions.
value: A personalised five-day path that answers their questions in context and checks understanding each day.
prompt: Using {enablement library}, build a 5-day plan for a new {segment} rep. Each day: 2 short videos, 1 practice task and 1 question they should be able to answer by the end of the day.
